rationale: REVISION 1 (council 66dbd0dd returned REVISE; editquality x2, bug_historian x3, guardian x3). Every objection accepted; two changed the plan materially. (1) bug_historian found a real defect I had copied deliberately: the existing empty_section verifier treats a MISSING component row as Resolved:true, but a missing row is the signature of this platform's most-repeated failure — a DELETE+INSERT rebuild silently removing a component. That verifier therefore cannot distinguish 'the defect was fixed' from 'the section was silently deleted', and I was about to propagate the blind spot to two more predicates while citing the precedent as justification. The revised plan FIXES it at source (edit 1) and the new verifiers inherit the corrected behaviour: an absent row now returns an ERROR, not Resolved:true, so the completion gate fails open exactly as before (the item still completes, nothing wedges) while result._verification records 'could not verify — target absent' instead of a false success. That converts a silent false-positive into a visible unknown. (2) image_url_404 is DROPPED. guardian flagged the outbound-HTTP latency on the completion path, and checking real volumes showed it has 4 items and 0 completions — so the one pick carrying novel risk had no volume to justify it. editquality was also right that 'highest-volume item type' was sloppy: hardcoded_section_colors is 180 items / 121 complete, the largest of my three but 8th overall (page_rerender is 1,898); the figures I quoted were a 30-day window presented as a total. (3) The verifiers.go comment-only edit is replaced by a FUNCTIONAL coverage guard plus a test, per bug_historian's point that a comment does not stop the next 46 item types self-reporting — the mitigation must fail loud, not read well. (4) A test for the extracted predicate is added, per guardian: check_hardcoded_section_colors.go has no test file, so an extraction refactor there would otherwise have no harness. ORIGINAL RATIONALE FOLLOWS. 'complete' on a work item means the handler saga returned success, not that the defect is gone. CLAUDE.md already enshrines this ('Trust the rendered artefact, not the status') and the platform has been bitten by it: robot-hands' gripper-detail product sections were marked complete on 2026-07-10 and were still serving empty markup on 2026-07-14. The fix for that case was built and is good — verifiers.go plus the completion gate in complete_work_item_verification.go. But only ONE verifier has ever been registered: RegisterVerifier("empty_section", ...) at check_empty_sections.go:38. Live 2026-07-19: of 4,570 complete items, exactly 5 carry a result._verification record, and 9 have ever reached 'verified' — all empty_section, none since 2026-07-14. A working, tested, already-wired safety mechanism covers one item type out of ~50; every other item type self-reports. Secondary motivation, stated so reviewers can weigh it: the reasoning-dataset workstream needs ground-truth outcome labels, and a verified/unknown/regressed distinction is worth far more as a training label than a self-reported complete — but the platform-quality argument stands on its own and is the reason to do it.

plan.summary: The completion-time verification framework is built, wired and proven, but has one verifier registered out of ~50 item types, so 4,565 of 4,570 complete items were never checked. Revision 1: first FIX the existing verifier's absent-row blind spot (a deleted component currently reads as 'resolved'), then register two more verifiers that inherit the corrected behaviour, add a test for the extracted predicate, and replace the proposed doc comment with a functional coverage guard that fails loud. image_url_404 dropped (4 items, 0 completions, and the only pick adding an outbound HTTP call to the completion path). No new tables, no schema change, no new LLM spend.

edits.rationale: THE BUG bug_historian found, fixed at source before anything copies it. Today an absent component row returns Resolved:true ('component no longer exists'), but that is precisely the signature of a DELETE+INSERT rebuild silently dropping the component — so a content-loss incident currently reads as a successful fix. Returning an error instead keeps behaviour identical from the item's point of view (the gate's documented policy is to fail OPEN on verifier error, so the item still completes and nothing wedges) while recording the ambiguity in result._verification. A silent false-positive becomes a visible unknown, which is the difference between data that misleads and data that is merely incomplete.
edits.sketch:
if err == sql.ErrNoRows {
-        // Component removed — nothing left to be empty.
-        return VerifyResult{Resolved: true, Detail: "component no longer exists"}, nil
+        // Component row absent. This is AMBIGUOUS and must not read as success:
+        // a missing row is equally the signature of a DELETE+INSERT rebuild
+        // silently dropping the component (the platform's most-repeated
+        // content-loss failure) as of a legitimate removal. Return an error so
+        // the completion gate fails OPEN (item completes, as before) while
+        // result._verification records that verification could not be made.
+        return VerifyResult{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot verify: component %s no longer exists (fixed or silently deleted — indistinguishable here)", componentID)
     }

edits.rationale: Largest of the candidate item types by real volume — 180 items, 121 complete (8th overall; the earlier 'highest-volume' phrasing was a 30-day window quoted as a total, and editquality was right to challenge it). Predicate is purely deterministic. Extracts the existing inline detection logic into a pure function called by BOTH the check and the verifier, so detection and verification cannot drift — the design intent verifiers.go already states. Inherits the corrected absent-row behaviour from edit 1.

Per guardian: this check has no test file, so extracting its predicate would be a behaviour-changing refactor with no harness. The test must lock the EXTRACTED function against the inline logic it replaces — table-driven over the same colour patterns the check's SQL/Go path matches today, following check_phantom_internal_links_test.go and check_empty_sections_test.go as the established pattern.
edits.sketch: Table-driven test over hardcodedColorVerdict covering, at minimum: inline style="color:#abc", inline background-color, a themed component using var(--...) (must NOT be flagged), an empty/whitespace body, and whatever exemptions the current inline predicate honours. Assert Resolved and that Detail names the offending pattern. The point is behaviour-identity with the pre-extraction predicate, so derive the cases from the existing detection code, not from first principles.

edits.rationale: 63 items, 37 complete. Deterministic DB lookup, and this file already has a test file so the extracted predicate has a harness. Inherits edit 1's corrected policy, which matters here for the same reason bug_historian gave: 'the link no longer exists on the page' must not read as success when a rebuild may have dropped the whole section containing it.

Replaces the comment-only edit the previous round proposed. bug_historian's objection was exactly right: patching 3 of ~50 call sites while the mechanism stays silently permissive is the same shape as the bug being fixed, and a doc comment does not stop the next 46. This exports the coverage gap as data so it can be asserted in a test (next edit) and reported on, rather than depending on the next author reading a comment.

The fail-loud half. An explicit allowlist of item_types knowingly without a verifier means adding a new check with no verifier BREAKS THE BUILD unless the author consciously adds it to the list. That is what stops recurrence; the previous round's comment would not have. The allowlist also becomes the honest, reviewable record of current coverage — today ~47 entries, and every one removed is a real improvement.

plan.risks: The dominant risk is a verifier wrong in the strict direction: returning Resolved:false for an item that is actually fixed burns an attempt and at max_attempts strands it in 'failed'. Each sketch therefore reuses the detection predicate rather than restating the rule, and every ambiguous case returns an ERROR (fail open) rather than false. Edit 1 changes the behaviour of a LIVE verifier: empty_section items whose component row has vanished will now complete-with-a-recorded-error instead of complete-as-verified. Net effect on item flow is nil (both complete), but the 'verified' population stops including cases we cannot actually verify — which is the point, and a reviewer should confirm nothing downstream reads result._verification.Resolved as a success signal. The extraction refactors must be behaviour-identical to the inline predicates they replace; edit 3 exists precisely because hardcoded_section_colors had no harness for that. phantom_internal_link's existing test file should be extended in the same way. The coverage test will FAIL on first run until the allowlist is populated with today's ~47 gaps — that is intended (it forces an honest inventory) but it means this cannot be merged half-done. Scope note: this still does NOT stamp status='verified'. No Go code sets that on site_work_items today, and introducing a new terminal status would touch the workItemTerminalStatuses / idx_swi_dedup lockstep that has caused fleet-wide 42P10. Evidence lands in result._verification, which is additive.
